source_text: Ἐνεργοὶ οὗτοι πάντες [οἱ] στρατιῶται καὶ φύλακες βέβαιοι. οὐδεὶς ἀργός, οὐδεὶς ἀχρεῖος. ὃ μὲν ἐξαιτήσασθαί σε δύναται παρὰ θεοῦ. ὅ δὲ παραμυθήσασθαι κάμνοντα, ὃ δὲ δακρῦσαι καὶ στενάξαι συμπαθῶς ὑπὲρ σοῦ πρὸς τὸν κύριον τῶν ὅλων, ὅ δὲ διδάξαι τι τῶν πρὸς τὴν σωτηρίαν χρησίμων, ὃ δὲ νουθετῆσαι μετὰ παρρησίας, ὃ δὲ συμβουλεῦσαι μετ᾿ εὐνοίας, πάντες δὲ φιλεῖν ἀληθῶς, ἀδόλως, ἀφόβως. ἀνυποκρίτως, ἀκολακεύτως. ἀπλάστως. ὦ γλυκεῖαι θεραπεῖαι φιλούντων, ὦ μακάριοι διακονίαι θαρρούντων, ὦ πίστις εἰλικρινὴς θεὸν μόνον δεδιότων, ὦ λόγων ἀλήθεια παρὰ τοῖς ψεύσασθαι μὴ δυναμένοις, ὦ κάλλος ἔργων παρὰ τοῖς θεῷ διακονεῖν πεπεισμένοις. πείθειν θεόν, ἀρέσκειν θεῷ· οὐ σαρκὸς τῆς σῆς ἅπτεσθαι δοκοῦσιν. ἀλλὰ τῆς ἑαυτοῦ ψυχῆς ἕκαστος, οὐκ ἀδελφῷ λαλεῖν, ἀλλὰ τῷ βασιλεῖ τῶν αἰώνων ἐν σοὶ κατοικοῦντι.
thought_title: The poor as effective soldiers and true friends
orientation: Clement is describing the poor believers whom the rich person has acquired as bodyguards, explaining what each one can do for the rich person before God.
pass_a_gloss: All these soldiers are effective and steadfast guards. No one is idle, no one is useless. One is able to obtain something for you from God by prayer. Another is able to comfort one who is weary, another to weep and groan with sympathy on your behalf before the Lord of all, another to teach something of the things useful for salvation, another to admonish with boldness, another to advise with goodwill, and all to love truly, without guile, without fear, without hypocrisy, without flattery, without pretense. O sweet services of those who love, O blessed ministries of those who are confident, O sincere faith of those who fear God alone, O truth of words among those who are not able to lie, O beauty of works among those who are persuaded to serve God. They seem not to touch your flesh, but each one touches his own soul, not to speak to a brother, but to the King of the ages dwelling in you.

lemmas.gloss: to obtain by asking, to pray for
one who is weary or sick

choices.term: Ἐνεργοὶ οὗτοι πάντες [οἱ] στρατιῶται καὶ φύλακες βέβαιοι
choices.english: All these soldiers are effective and steadfast guards
choices.why: Keeps the military metaphor from the previous section and renders the predicate adjectives as a single assertion about the group
rejected: All these soldiers and guards are active and reliable

choices.english: is able to obtain something for you from God by prayer
choices.why: ἐξαιτέω means to ask for and obtain, and παρὰ θεοῦ marks the source; the gloss makes the prayer sense explicit
τῶν ὅλων means all things, the universe; a standard divine title

choices.english: without hypocrisy, without flattery, without pretense
choices.why: The three adverbs are rendered as parallel prepositional phrases to preserve the rhetorical rhythm and each distinct nuance

choices.term: οὐ σαρκὸς τῆς σῆς ἅπτεσθαι δοκοῦσιν, ἀλλὰ τῆς ἑαυτοῦ ψυχῆς ἕκαστος
choices.english: They seem not to touch your flesh, but each one touches his own soul
choices.why: Preserves the contrast between flesh and soul and the distributive force of ἕκαστος
rejected: They do not seem to touch your flesh, but each his own soul

choices.term: τῷ βασιλεῖ τῶν αἰώνων ἐν σοὶ κατοικοῦντι
choices.english: to the King of the ages dwelling in you
choices.why: τῶν αἰώνων is a standard divine title; the participle κατοικοῦντι is rendered as a relative clause to keep the syntax clear
rejected: to the King of eternity who dwells in you

pass_b_english: All these soldiers are effective and steadfast guards. None is idle, none is useless. One is able to obtain something for you from God. Another can comfort the weary. Another can weep and groan with sympathy for you before the Lord of all. Another can teach you something useful for salvation. Another can admonish you with boldness. Another can counsel you with goodwill. And all of them can love truly—without deceit, without fear, without hypocrisy, without flattery, without pretense.

O sweet services of those who love! O blessed ministries of those who have confidence! O sincere faith of those who fear God alone! O truth of words among those who cannot lie! O beauty of deeds among those who are persuaded to serve God! They persuade God, they please God. They seem not to touch your flesh, but each one, concerning his own soul, does not speak to a brother, but to the King of the ages dwelling in you.
